rv.q: 'Black Girl from a White Suburb' isn't the most dramatic or profound memoir-style show that I've seen, but its very ordinariness gives it an undeniable ring of truth.
Black Girl from a White Suburb is a must-see, in my book.

Richard, who also has discussed race and identity in her podcast, Tania’s Take , and in other media outlets, does know how to connect with her audience, which on the night I attended was mostly older white people.
It's because of powerful moments like these that I'm left wanting more.

Black Girl From a White Suburb is a phenomenal piece of writing because it takes a whole woman's life, packed with lessons, social commentary, and nostalgia and hits it all succinctly in just a one hour show.
While I liked the production a lot, it could have been maybe five or ten minutes longer to further explore how Richard found her own light (as in the subtitle of her book).
